name: West Cliff @ Steamer Lane
footage_note: Archived Surfline cliff cam — real fixed camera at this exact site; archived feed, not a live unit.
_disarmed_note: velocity_anomaly is implemented but disarmed here: on surf footage every wave ride is a speed spike, measured at 98 false fires in 180s. Illustrative only, not a validated capability.
agent_context: Unpatrolled cliff break on West Cliff Drive. Surfers regularly sit inside the rock impact zone at the north end of the lineup, where a set wave can push a surfer onto exposed rock. Nearest lifeguard tower is seasonal and 2.3 miles south. Cliff access to the waterline is via a single stair with no vehicle access; a shore rescue requires Harbor Patrol by water.

name: Downtown Pedestrian Corridor
footage_note: Public boardwalk webcam used as stand-in for a downtown Santa Cruz corridor. Real fixed surveillance-style camera; not this location.
agent_context: Downtown pedestrian corridor adjacent to a vendor market. Heavy foot traffic during daytime hours; corridor is posted closed overnight. Ground-level medical incidents here are most commonly heat exhaustion, intoxication, or overdose. Nearest patrol unit is 0.4 miles; Fire/EMS station is 0.9 miles with direct street access.

name: Harbor Entrance — Day Watch
footage_note: santacruzharbor.org live webcam (HD Relay) — recorded live 2026-07-26 ~11:40 PDT via 1 fps snapshot polling.
agent_context: Santa Cruz Harbor entrance channel in daylight. Kayakers and paddleboarders share the narrow channel with powered vessels; a person in the water here is exposed to boat traffic and the jetty rocks on both sides. Harbor Patrol is stationed inside the harbor with a fast response boat. A person-sized detection dwelling in the channel is more likely a paddler than a swimmer — say so, and weight urgency accordingly.

name: Harbor Entrance — Night Watch
footage_note: santacruzharbor.org live webcam (HD Relay) — recorded live 2026-07-25 ~22:15 PDT via 1 fps snapshot polling. Night/IR view; quiet by design.
agent_context: Santa Cruz Harbor entrance channel at night. After hours there are no lifeguards; Harbor Patrol is on call inside the harbor. Person detections at night are rare and low-confidence — treat any person in the channel or on the jetty as high urgency, but state the low-light CV uncertainty plainly in the dispatch summary.

name: Main Beach — South Panorama
footage_note: WebCOOS Walton Lighthouse camera, second preset — real fixed camera viewing Main Beach and the Boardwalk; archived 2026-07-25 15:41 PDT.
agent_context: Wide southern panorama of Main Beach and the Boardwalk from the harbor mouth. Heaviest tourist swim traffic in Santa Cruz; multiple rescues on summer weekends. Lifeguard coverage concentrated near the Boardwalk towers thins toward the river mouth end of the frame. Waders far from a tower who stay in the surf line are the primary concern.

name: Seabright Beach @ Harbor Mouth
footage_note: WebCOOS Walton Lighthouse camera (UCSC/SECOORA) — real fixed camera at this exact site; archived feed from 2026-07-25 15:36 PDT.
agent_context: Seabright State Beach at the Santa Cruz harbor mouth. The jetty creates strong lateral currents and a known rip along the rock line; waders near the channel can be pulled toward the harbor shipping lane. Seasonal lifeguard tower on the beach, staffed summer daytime only. Harbor Patrol is adjacent inside the harbor; State Parks lifeguards respond on the beach side. People climbing the jetty rip-rap are a recurring injury source.

name: Municipal Wharf @ Main Beach
footage_note: WebCOOS Santa Cruz Wharf camera (CeNCOOS) — real fixed camera at this exact site; archived feed from 2026-07-25 15:39 PDT.
agent_context: Municipal Wharf camera over Main Beach, the busiest beach in the city, directly beside the Boardwalk. Summer crowds in the thousands; lifeguard towers staffed daytime. Rip currents form along the wharf pilings and swimmers drift toward them. City Fire marine rescue launches from the wharf; response time to the surf line is short but the crowd density makes spotting a single person in trouble hard — exactly what automated watch is for.
